data.hypothesis: Combining the 512-source shared-memory tile with two outputs per thread may amortize cooperative source loading across more targets. Extra registers and fewer CTAs may offset that benefit; this candidate is unmeasured.

memory_lessons.applicability: The shared-tile and two-output strategies may complement each other, but standalone timings do not predict their combined performance.
memory_lessons.claim: The 512-source shared-memory integration passed correctness at 0.00112490 s, while the correct two-output candidate was slower alone at 0.00274554 s. The combined candidate needs independent measurement.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Run the full correctness suite and official timing protocol on the combined candidate; retain the 512-tile candidate if it fails or is slower.

data.notes: The two targets per thread are first and first + blockDim.x, matching block=256 and items_per_block=512. All threads participate in both shared-memory barriers, including inactive tail threads. Each target retains ascending source order, the original force expression, update order, and exact mass via copying its Particle state. The only evidence of performance so far is for the 512-tile base and the separate two-output variant; this combination requires fresh correctness and measurement.
transformations: Stage each 512-source tile cooperatively in shared memory and reuse it across the block.
Assign two target particles per thread at first and first + blockDim.x, maintaining separate accumulators and guarded outputs.
Set items_per_block=512 with block=256; keep all threads participating in tile barriers and preserve per-target source accumulation order.
